sentences.text: Shri Vijay Dutta Sharma, learned counsel for the appe  Shri Ajay Kumar Nirankari-learned Public Prosecutor f State.
Heard on I.A.No. 8674/2024, 8th repeat application under Section 389(1) of Cr.P.C. for suspension of sentence and grant of bail moved on behalf of appellant.

Present appellant stands convicted under Section 376(g) of IPC and sentenced to undergo Life Imprisonment with fine of Rs.2000/-, under Section 506(B) of IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I.
for 2 years with fine of Rs.500/-, under Section 342 of IPC and sentenced to undergo 6 months R.I.
with fine of Rs.500/-, Section 377 of the IPC and sentenced to undergo ten years RI with fine of Rs.
1000/-, Section 3(a)/4 of POCSO Act and sentenced to undergo ten years RI with fine of Rs. 1000/-
& under Section 67(KHA) of IT Act and sentenced to undergo 2 years R.I. with fine of Rs.300/- with default stipulations vide judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 30/07/2013 passed passed in Sessions Trial No.16/2013 by Special Judge, Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities Act) and Additional Sessions Judge, District Datia.
Present appellant so far has already undergone jail sentence of more than 10 years and 10 months without remission.
As per prosecution story, on 6/10/2012, prosecutrix made an application to the Police Station Bhander that on 01/10/2012, at about 7:30 p.m., she was 2 CRA-675-2013 going to bring firewood for cooking the food and when she reached near the house of one Sita Ram Mukhariya, accused person Neetu Sengar and Abhishek came there and took her in a house which was situated in nearby street where other accused persons namely Sandesh Yadav, Lucky Yadav, Kaushal Kishore and Ashu Pathan were already present.
Thereafter, the prosecurix was forced to be naked and then, all the accused persons committed rape with the prosecutrix.

It is further alleged that accused persons namely Sandesh and Abhishek prepared a video (film) of the alleged incident and threatened her to spoil his life, if she told anything about the alleged incident to anyone.

On such information, FIR was registered against the present appellant along with other co-accused persons and investigation Sumit Gangotiya vs State Of M.P. on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113430060/
1 was set in motion.

sentences.text: Upon completion of investigation including recording of statements, collection of evidence and necessary formalities, challan was filed.
The Special Court on appreciation of evidence placed on record convicted and sentenced the present appellant, as aforesaid.
Learned Counsel for the appellant, while taking exception to the impugned judgment of conviction and order of sentence, submits that present appellant is innocent and has been falsely implicated.
The Special Court has not appreciated the evidence placed on record in correct perspective.
The judgment suffers from surmises and conjectures.
It is further submitted that there is delay of 5 days in registration of FIR and the DNA report of present appellant is found negative.

Learned counsel for appellant further submits that he prays for suspension of sentence solely on the ground of long incarceration suffered by present appellant as he has already suffered actual incarceration of more 10 years and 10 months without remission.
It is also submitted that the co-accused Lucky Yadav and Kaushal Kishore have already been granted benefit of 3 CRA-675-2013 suspension of jail sentence.
That apart, the appeal is of the year 2013 and there is no likelihood of early hearing of the appeal in the near future.
Hence, prays for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to present appellant solely on the ground of long incarceration.

Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor while supporting the judgment impugned, submits that no exception can be taken in the matter of suspension of sentence and grant of bail to present appellant looking to the nature and the gravity of offence.

Upon hearing learned counsel for the parties, though this Court is not inclined to extend the benefit of suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the present appellant on merits, however, regard being had to the fact that present appellant so far has already suffered incarceration of more than 10 years and 10 months without remission coupled with the fact that the appeal is pending since 2013 is not likely to be decided in the near future, in the obtaining facts and circumstances, present appellant is entitled to the benefit of suspension of sentence and grant of bail.

Accordingly, I.A.No. 8674/2024 stands allowed and it is directed that the jail sentence of appellant- Sumit Gangotiya shall remain suspended during pendency of the present appeal and he shall be released on bail subject to verification of the factum of depositing the fine amount and on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.2,00,000/- (Rupees Two Lac only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Trial Court subject to verification of factum regarding deposit of fine amount.
Present appellant is directed to appear before the Registry of this Court first on 12/11/2024 and thereafter, on other subsequent dates as may be fixed in this 4 CRA-675-2013 behalf.
Accordingly, the said IA stands allowed and disposed of.
Observations on facts, if any, are only for the purpose of deciding the instant I.A. and shall have no bearing on the merits of the appeal.
